view: The +31.48% reinstatement day repriced the governance discount, not the business. The Q3 FY27 numbers and the $130B Q4 guide are unchanged. At 165.05 NVDA trades at about 11x forward EPS (derived) and 20.6x TTM, against 75% forecast growth. It is still cheap if the reported numbers are reliable, but it is no longer the 8.4x panic price. In my slice the SEC accounting question, the unfiled Q3 10-Q (deadline about 2026-12-04) and the $118B of guarantees are all unresolved. They now carry the downside, and the 125.53-156.93 gap is open below.

But the late-Feb 2027 print and the remote-access licence deadline (about 2027-02-17) fall inside the window, and an SEC review rarely resolves within a quarter. this_quarter: base 39/43/18 becomes 34/33/33. Six weeks is not long for fundamentals to re-rate, while a 10-Q or probe disclosure can move price at any time.

Growth is unchanged since the 11-22 run. Q3 FY27 revenue was $115.84B: +103% YoY, +20% QoQ, 6.5% above the $108.73B estimate. Data center was $107.6B (+110% YoY), about 92.9% of revenue. Adj EPS 2.68 vs 2.47 est (+8.5%). GAAP net income $65.3B is about a 56% net margin (derived). The next-FY growth forecast is 75%. Nothing new on the business arrived with the reinstatement.

Margins: GAAP gross 74.8%, adjusted 74.9%, operating 66.9%. The Q4 gross-margin guide of 71-72% (Vera Rubin ramp) is about 3.4 points lower at the midpoint. That is the first margin number to check in late Feb.

Valuation vs its own growth at 165.05. P/E TTM is 20.62, which implies TTM EPS of about 8.00 (derived). Annualised last-quarter adj EPS of 10.72 (2.68 x 4) gives about 15.4x (derived). Forward P/E: the slice still shows 8.4, but that is the 125.53 figure carried unrescaled (pe_ttm was rescaled, fwd_pe was not). Implied forward EPS is about 14.94 (125.53 / 8.4), so forward P/E at 165.05 is about 11.0x (derived). P/S TTM is not in the slice. Market cap $3.98T is about 8.6x annualised Q3 revenue ($463B) and about 7.7x the annualised Q4 guide ($520B), both derived. A PEG near 0.15 is still far below a normal multiple for 75% growth. The re-rating so far is from 8.4x to 11x; it is not yet a growth multiple.

Earnings setup. The 2026-11-17 print has passed; the next print is late Feb 2027 (date not confirmed) and falls inside next_quarter. The bar is the Q4 guide of $130B +/-3% (floor about $126.1B), 4.2% above the $124.8B consensus. It assumes zero China data-center compute revenue (last quarter China Hopper was $2.4B, about 2.1% of revenue), plus gross margin of 71-72%. Before vs after (rule 9): the beat-and-raise on 11-17 did not lift the stock (162.85 to 145.98 by Thursday), and the reinstatement did, with no new numbers. In this regime the stock trades on credibility and governance, not on beats. A late-Feb beat with a clean 10-Q history would likely be worth more than the 11-17 beat. A miss below $126.1B, or gross margin below 71%, would hit an 11x stock that has already re-rated 31%.

Balance sheet. Guarantees are $118B (prior $108.5B, +$9.5B). $105B is a single OpenAI Ohio campus guarantee, and $0 has been paid. Cash and securities are $53.5B, so guarantees are 2.2x cash. Q3 FCF and total debt are NOT in the slice, so I cannot check the latest-quarter debt and FCF swings asked for. This is the third run with that gap. Capital calls stacked on cash: a boosted buyback, the planned $12.9B Hugging Face purchase under DOJ review, and the guarantees.

notes_for_chair: Rebound post-mortem, part 1: signs before 2026-11-23 (inputs/readings_2026-11-22.json) that POINTED to a sharp rebound. (a) Valuation stretch: 8.4x forward and about 11.7x annualised reported EPS on 75% forecast growth (PEG about 0.1). That gave the magnitude: the move re-rated to about 11x, about what one catalyst could produce. (b) The business was intact: a beat-and-raise ($115.84B vs $108.73B est; guide $130B vs $124.8B), a guide that assumed zero China, and 0/4 hyperscaler capex cuts. (c) FY Jan-2028 EPS estimates up about 23% in 90 days (TIKR, news_governance), with a median PT of 222.5, 77% above 125.53. (d) Boosted buyback. (e) The only sign of the actual catalyst: Huang said he would be 'honored' to return. (f) The conditional 2w drop <= -15% table (n=4: 50 up / 50 range / 0 down) and capitulation-type volume on 11-20 (3.9x average, close 0.8% above the low) suggested an exhausted seller. These are technical and sentiment items, outside my lane. (g) AAII bearish 51.4 (stale).

Rebound post-mortem, part 2: signs that DID NOT point to it. (a) The board said the opposite: Chair Harvey Jones said Huang would not be reinstated, and the board had hired Heidrick & Struggles. (b) Treasury Secretary Bessent urged an outside CEO and a 'dramatic shakeup'. (c) Reuters 11-20 on an SEC enforcement review of accounting; the 10-Q not filed, unlike the last three quarters. (d) The BIS remote-access rule (TB3 candidate). (e) Guarantees up to $118B. (f) Downgrades (Summit to Hold; Wells Fargo PT cut). (g) The 11-17 beat had failed to lift the stock. (h) Congressional testimony requests for 12-01 to 12-03. Honest summary: fundamentals said the stock was cheap and gave the size of the move, but nothing in my evidence predicted the trigger or its timing. The trigger was a governance reversal that the latest board statement had denied. My 11-22 forecast was 2w 34/30/36 (up threshold 131.81). It is now deep in 'up' on the 2026-12-04 measure (165.05 = +31.5%) if it holds, and I had a slight down tilt. Proposed lessons-log line: 'When a drawdown is governance-driven with intact fundamentals and extreme multiples, the reversal tail is fat. Do not tilt 2w down on governance news alone; keep up >= down when forward P/E is at a multi-year low.'

Cross-lane (TB2): the 11-12 chair ruled TB2 FIRED (owner not confirmed). The CEO is now back as President, CEO and director, so the departure that fired TB2 is reversed. The chair and owner should rule whether TB2 clears. Separately, the SEC accounting question is not covered by TB1-TB4. My candidate TB5 (accounting integrity: formal SEC investigation disclosure, restatement, delayed periodic filing, or auditor resignation or qualified opinion) remains a proposal, owner approval required. My slice does not say whether the reinstatement changes the SEC review or the requested 12-01/12-03 testimony (status 'not confirmed').

Expected (not triggers): ex-dividend 2026-12-02; Q3 10-Q deadline about 2026-12-04 (what matters is on time vs late, and what it discloses); FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10, both just after the 2w date; licence deadline about 2027-02-17; Q4 FY27 print late Feb 2027, inside next_quarter. The outcome thresholds are in what_would_change_my_mind.

Stance (fundamentals lens, proposal only; the owner decides; no orders): strategic Accumulate is still supported by valuation (about 11x forward, 75% growth, demand intact) once TB2 is formally cleared. I would keep a 'credibility tranche' (for example a third of budget) gated on a clean Q3 10-Q, not on price. Tactical: Wait through about 2026-12-04. A +31% day into an open gap, with the 10-Q binary inside two weeks, is a poor point to chase. Accumulate/Wait proposals for ladder rows are for the owner; ladder levels anchored to forward-EPS multiples (10x = 149.4, 12x = 179.3) should be re-marked to consensus each run.
